plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and cure the mandate breach.
Increase QQQI to 25% to favor income and broad index exposure for stability.

conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for a target of ~1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, leading to lower expected drawdowns. Returns will be modest, but the portfolio is better positioned for stability.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, SPAL to 2%, MUU to 3%, and METU to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and cure the mandate breach.

This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some tech exposure while reducing overall leverage.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% per month, aiming for risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech. Expect moderate drawdowns, with a focus on sustainable growth.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to cure the concentration breach while maintaining broad exposure.
Add to SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to 7%, 6%, 6%, and 6% respectively, leaning into leveraged tech.
Buy META at 8% as a high-scoring new tech setup.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretch growth by leveraging high-scoring setups. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs, which can lead to larger drawdowns and daily decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the elevated risk.

plan: Sell SOXL, SPAL, MUU, and METU to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.
Trim CRWD to 5% and SNOW to 1% to reduce high-beta single name exposure.
Add to QQQI to 30% to rotate into income-focused ETFs for steady distributions.

income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It significantly reduces leverage and high-beta names, favoring income-generating ETFs. While aiming for steady distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are not guaranteed.
